description: An introduction to presentation software used to create and display slide-based shows, covering slides, layouts, templates, themes, inserting objects, animations, transitions and tips for effective presentations.

mcq.questionText: What is the main purpose of presentation software?

options.text: To perform calculations on numbers in cells
To create slides for displaying information to an audience
To edit and retouch digital photographs
To send and receive electronic mail

mcq.explanation: Presentation software is designed to create a series of slides that present information visually to an audience.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of presentation software?
mcq.explanation: Microsoft PowerPoint is a widely used presentation program, while the others are a spreadsheet, an image editor and a web browser.

mcq.questionText: Which free and open-source program is part of LibreOffice and used to make presentations?
mcq.explanation: LibreOffice Impress is the presentation component, while Writer is for documents, Calc for spreadsheets and Base for databases.

mcq.questionText: What is a single page in a presentation called?
mcq.explanation: Each individual page in a presentation is called a slide, and a collection of slides forms the whole presentation.

mcq.questionText: What does a slide layout determine?

options.text: The colour of the desktop background
The arrangement of placeholders for text and objects on a slide
The speed of the computer processor
The number of files saved on the disk

mcq.explanation: A slide layout defines how placeholders for titles, text, pictures and other content are positioned on a slide.

mcq.questionText: What is a theme in presentation software?

options.text: A set of coordinated colours, fonts and effects applied to slides
A tool for checking spelling mistakes
A method of saving a file to a flash disk

mcq.explanation: A theme is a predefined combination of colours, fonts and visual effects that gives a presentation a consistent look.

mcq.questionText: Which feature controls how one slide changes to the next during a slide show?
mcq.explanation: A transition is the visual effect that occurs when moving from one slide to the next, such as fade or wipe.

mcq.questionText: What is an animation in a presentation?

options.text: A movement or visual effect applied to objects on a slide
The act of printing all slides as handouts
The process of saving the presentation online
A way of password-protecting a file

mcq.explanation: An animation is an effect that makes text or objects on a slide move, appear or disappear during the show.

mcq.questionText: Which view starts displaying the presentation full screen to an audience?
mcq.explanation: Slide Show view presents the slides full screen, one after another, for the audience to watch.

mcq.questionText: What is the benefit of using a template when creating a presentation?

options.text: It provides a ready-made design and structure to start from
It increases the speed of the internet connection
It converts the slides into a spreadsheet

mcq.explanation: A template is a pre-designed file with layouts and formatting that saves time and ensures consistency.

mcq.questionText: Why might a presenter insert a chart into a slide?

options.text: To display numerical data in a clear, visual way
To check the grammar of the text
To connect the computer to a printer

mcq.explanation: Charts turn numbers into visual graphics such as bars or pie slices, making data easier for the audience to understand.

mcq.questionText: Which keyboard key is commonly used to start a slide show from the beginning in PowerPoint?
mcq.explanation: Pressing F5 starts the slide show from the first slide, while Esc ends the show.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a good tip for designing an effective presentation?

options.text: Fill every slide with long paragraphs of text
Use short bullet points and readable fonts
Use many different fonts and colours on each slide
Add as many animations as possible on every word

mcq.explanation: Effective slides use brief bullet points and clear, large fonts so the audience can read and follow easily.

mcq.questionText: What is the purpose of the slide master in presentation software?

options.text: To control the design and formatting of all slides at once
To delete the last slide automatically
To scan the document for viruses
To translate text into another language

mcq.explanation: The slide master stores formatting that applies to every slide, so changes made there affect the whole presentation.

mcq.questionText: In which file format is a Microsoft PowerPoint presentation commonly saved by default?
mcq.explanation: PowerPoint presentations are saved with the .pptx extension, while .docx is for Word and .xlsx for Excel.

fib.questionText: A single page within a presentation is called a _____.
fib.explanation: Slides are the individual pages that together make up a presentation.

fib.questionText: The presentation program included in the Microsoft Office suite is Microsoft _____.
fib.explanation: Microsoft PowerPoint is the best known presentation application.

fib.questionText: The presentation program in the LibreOffice suite is called _____.
fib.explanation: LibreOffice Impress is a free alternative for creating presentations.

fib.questionText: The visual effect that occurs when changing from one slide to the next is called a _____.
fib.explanation: Transitions add movement between slides during the show.

fib.questionText: An effect applied to make text or objects move on a slide is called an _____.
fib.explanation: Animations control how objects enter, exit or move on a slide.

fib.questionText: A predefined set of coordinated colours, fonts and effects applied to slides is called a _____.
fib.explanation: Themes give a presentation a consistent professional appearance.

fib.questionText: The arrangement of placeholders for content on a slide is determined by the slide _____.
fib.explanation: The layout decides where titles, text and images appear on a slide.

fib.questionText: A ready-made design file used as a starting point for new presentations is called a _____.
fib.explanation: Templates provide preset layouts and formatting to save time.

fib.questionText: Displaying the slides full screen to an audience is known as running a slide _____.
fib.explanation: A slide show plays the slides one after another in full screen.

fib.questionText: A graphical representation of numerical data, such as a bar or pie graph inserted into a slide, is called a _____.
fib.explanation: Charts make numerical information easier to understand visually.

tf.questionText: Presentation software is mainly used to create slides for sharing information with an audience.
tf.explanation: This is the core purpose of presentation programs.

tf.questionText: Microsoft Excel is an example of presentation software.
tf.explanation: Microsoft Excel is spreadsheet software; PowerPoint is the presentation program in Office.

tf.questionText: A transition is the effect used when moving from one slide to the next.
tf.explanation: Transitions control the visual change between slides.

tf.questionText: An animation is applied to control how objects move or appear on a single slide.
tf.explanation: Animations affect objects within a slide, unlike transitions which act between slides.

tf.questionText: Putting large amounts of text on every slide makes a presentation more effective.
tf.explanation: Too much text crowds slides; short bullet points are clearer and more effective.

tf.questionText: LibreOffice Impress is a free presentation program.
tf.explanation: Impress is the free, open-source presentation tool in LibreOffice.

tf.questionText: A theme determines the coordinated colours and fonts used throughout a presentation.
tf.explanation: Themes provide a consistent set of colours, fonts and effects.

tf.questionText: You can insert images and charts into slides to support your message.
tf.explanation: Slides can hold text, pictures, charts and other objects.

tf.questionText: A slide layout cannot be changed once a slide has been created.
tf.explanation: The layout of a slide can be changed at any time to suit the content.

tf.questionText: Pressing the Esc key during a running slide show will end the presentation.
tf.explanation: The Esc key stops the slide show and returns to the editing view.

hoq.questionText: A teacher prepares a science lesson with many full sentences on each slide, five different fonts, and an animation on every single word. The students find it hard to follow. Which change would most improve the presentation?

options.text: Replace long sentences with short bullet points and reduce the number of fonts and animations
Add even more animations so the slides look livelier
Increase the number of fonts to seven for variety
Remove all images and charts from the slides

hoq.explanation: Effective slides are simple: short bullet points, consistent fonts and limited animation help the audience follow the message.

hoq.questionText: A student wants every slide in a 30-slide presentation to show the school logo in the same corner and use the same title font, without editing each slide one by one. What is the best way to do this?

options.text: Edit the slide master so the logo and font apply to all slides
Manually copy and paste the logo onto all 30 slides
Add a different transition to each slide
Save the file in a spreadsheet format

hoq.explanation: The slide master holds formatting and objects that appear on every slide, so editing it once updates all slides.

hoq.questionText: A presenter has a table of monthly sales figures and wants the audience to quickly see which month had the highest sales. Which approach communicates this most effectively on a slide?

options.text: Insert a bar chart that visually compares the monthly figures
Paste the raw numbers in a small font filling the slide
Read all the numbers aloud without any visual
Add a sound effect to each number

hoq.explanation: A chart turns numbers into a visual comparison, letting the audience instantly spot the highest value.
